page.layout: One printed page, one block of text: a centred title heading at the top, then a verse poem in italic lines with a large initial H, a signature line below the poem, and a gathering signature at the foot. No margin notes.

l.i: Nos Christi insignem multa pietate ministrum,
Qui viuens docuit nos rectè viuere: mundo
Excedens docuit nos, benè posse mori.
Eximia hæc laus est: quam si quis captat, eodem
Ad metam cursu, quo VVidebramus, eat.
Quem ceu voce prius, sic nunc evulgo libellis,
Idq; sub auspicijs MENS GENEROSA tuis.
Vt cuius tumulus, tumulumq; sequentia Sacra
Ille tuas laudes atque ornamenta vicissim
Augere, & toto spargere in orbe queat:
Sicq; nouo exemplo, ostendat, post funera gratus,
Ingrati quonam mens sit habenda loco.

page.notes: The large initial H of the first verse line is set as a woodcut-style drop capital and is joined to the word "ector"; the reading "Hectora" is given as printed. The line "Quem ceu voce prius" and the signature "Barth. Pitiscus." are set in italic; the gathering mark "A 2" is at the lower right and is written as a signature, not text. Some letters in the poem (e.g. "Idq;", "Sicq;") are rendered with the q-abbreviation as printed.
